title: Wicked tenants kill the heir; vineyard given to others
english: On the parable of the farmers. The people’s wise ones, seeing the Son, take him for the heir and dare to kill him to own the vineyard. They cast him out and kill him; then the vineyard’s Lord arrives, [[raised from the dead >> Bible:Matthew 21:38-41]], destroys the bad farmers badly, and hands the vineyard to other farmers — the apostles. He answers from prophecy that he was rejected by them yet is precious with God and [[head of the corner >> Bible:Psalm 118:22]]; [[the kingdom of God will be taken from you and given to a nation producing its fruits >> Bible:Matthew 21:43]].
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B.
Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: When God is called man, householder, or king
english: Compare the parables where God is called a man. In the laborers he is a [[householder hiring at dawn >> Bible:Matthew 20:1]]; in the supper and the son’s wedding he is named a [[king >> Bible:Matthew 22:2]] — greater than a householder, as one who sends an army. Luke and Mark say a man planted a vineyard. In the Scriptures God is taken as ‘man’ in many ways; it matters greatly whether he is named simply man, householder, or king. Glory to Christ. Amen.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B.
Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
